title: Northway Bank - Data residency & compliance discovery
summary: Initial discovery for data residency and logging requirements. Customer requires EU data residency for customer PII and financial records, SOC2+HIPAA considerations for certain products, strict audit log retention, and options for private deployment (VPC/on-prem). Discussed Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and next steps for a pilot and security questionnaire.
topics: Data residency (EU) for PII and transaction logs
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options
next_steps: Redwood: Share SOC2 + HIPAA mapping and security pack (Ava) by 2026-03-06
Customer: Send network topology and list of in-scope data flows (Ellen) by 2026-03-11
Schedule pilot kickoff for Dedicated capacity benchmark (Marco/Ellen) week of 2026-03-16
action_items: Ava Martinez — send SOC2 report, Data Processing Agreement, and HIPAA flow mapping — 2026-03-06
Ellen Price — provide network diagram, where logs currently land, and regulatory scope per product — 2026-03-11
Marco Chen — prepare Dedicated benchmark plan and cost estimate — 2026-03-12
transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Ava from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. Marco from our SE team will cover the technical bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Ellen: Good, thanks. Running a bit late but all good, Ellen here, Head of Cloud Ops at Northway.
[00:12] Marcus: Marcus Hale, CISO, I'll jump in on security questions.
[00:16] Priya: Priya Singh, compliance.
[00:20] Marco: Hi all, Marco Chen, systems engineer. Quick agenda — understand your residency and compliance needs, current stack, and discuss hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private). We'll recap next steps.
[00:32] Ava: Great, Ellen could you give us the use cases you plan to run against Redwood? Which products will touch customer data?
[00:38] Ellen: Sure, we have two primary flows. One is a customer support summarization feature that will ingest PII — names, partial account numbers, sometimes SSNs for identity verification; second is internal fraud detection where transaction data gets passed for risk scoring. Both are in-scope for stricter controls.
[00:56] Priya: To add, for the support flow we need EU data residency for EU customers and also long-term retention rules for audit trails. We need to map where logs live, retention and masking.
[01:12] Ava: Understood. Are you evaluating Hosted (Redwood API) or Dedicated/Private to meet residency?
[01:18] Ellen: Initially we were hoping hosted could work but our security team is concerned about logs leaving region and multitenancy. So Dedicated or Private are on the table.
[01:28] Marcus: Right, key concerns: data residency (we need EU region for EU PII), audit logs with immutable retention, KMS control for encryption, SOC 2 evidence and HIPAA mapping for a subset of flows. Also SSO/SAML integration and RBAC.
[01:44] Marco: Thanks. Quick clarifying q — when you say EU residency do you mean both at-rest storage and any transient logs/metrics?
[01:50] Priya: Yes. Both. We want request payloads and generated outputs for EU users to never leave EU, and logs that might include metadata (timestamps, user ids) must be retained in-region.
[02:02] Ava: That's common. For Hosted we support regional endpoints but some of our shared infra routes telemetry to central services — that's where customers bump into control gaps. Dedicated gives you dedicated GPU pools in a region with stronger isolation, and Private gives you full customer-managed VPC or on-prem for the strictest needs.
[02:22] Ellen: Can you clarify logs specifically — what types of logs do you keep, and can retention be limited? We have regulatory limits that require 7 years for certain financial records.
[02:34] Marco: We collect several categories: request/response transcripts (if enabled), system-level logs (errors, infra metrics), and operational audit logs (who called what, API keys used). By default Hosted keeps short retention for transcripts and metrics, but Dedicated/Private allow configurable retention and options for forwarding to your log storage (S3 in-region, SIEM). We can support longer retention windows and hooking into your KMS for encryption of logs at rest.
[02:59] Marcus: Who controls the KMS keys in Dedicated vs Private? We have a hard requirement that keys for EU PII must be customer-managed.
[03:08] Marco: For Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) so you control keys used for data at rest in the dedicated cluster. For Private (VPC or on-prem) you fully control the key lifecycle; the control plane can be configured to use your KMS endpoints.
[03:24] Priya: On HIPAA — certain support flows will be PHI if they include health-related notes. Does Redwood sign a BAA and support HIPAA-compliant configurations?
[03:34] Ava: We do sign BAAs for Private deployments and for Dedicated with proper contractual addenda. We'll share our HIPAA mapping. For Hosted we typically do not take PHI unless under special agreement and controls.
[03:46] Ellen: What's the typical timeline to get Dedicated spun up for a pilot? We want to run latency and cost benchmarks.
[03:54] Marco: Typically 2-4 weeks for a pilot environment once network connectivity (VPC peering, private link) is established. We can pre-provision capacity for benching.
[04:04] Marcus: About logging restrictions — sometimes our regulators require that certain fields never appear in logs even in masked form. Can you guarantee PII fields won't be persisted to logs for in-scope flows?
[04:16] Marco: We have masking at ingestion that can drop or redact fields, and the runtime supports prefix caching so not all content is logged. For Dedicated/Private we can turn off transcript logging entirely for in-scope routes and route audit logs to your collector. We should document exactly which API fields get logged.
[04:36] Priya: Good; also need to know whether we can get immutable audit trails — write once logs?
[04:42] Ava: We can forward to your object store with lifecycle policies and use write-once buckets or write-once governance in your SIEM. For the Redwood-managed side, we can provide tamper-evident logs and export signatures. We'll include details in the security pack.
[04:59] Ellen: On residency: if we use Dedicated in eu-west-1, all inference runs and cache storage will stay in region?
[05:07] Marco: Yes, Dedicated is region pinned. Network egress for telemetry can be configured to stay in-region. One caveat: control plane operations (billing/console) sometimes call central services — we can offer a private control plane for Private customers.
[05:21] Marcus: Ok how about model variants and fallbacks — if capacity is constrained you mentioned fallbacks to smaller models. Could that cause data to leave region if fallback model lives elsewhere?
[05:31] Marco: Great question. Our smart routing can be region-aware; for Dedicated we do not route in-region requests out. For Hosted, fallbacks could cross-region. We'll make sure fallbacks for Dedicated stay within pinned region or we can enforce hard policies that refuse cross-region fallback.
[05:50] Ellen: What about SSO and RBAC? We need SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning.
[05:55] Ava: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning across Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SAML for org logins but SCIM provisioning on Hosted is limited for multi-tenant orgs; we'll share the exact capabilities.
[06:08] Priya: Please share your SOC 2 scope and if there are any outstanding exceptions.
[06:12] Ava: We'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and a controls matrix. We also have an ISO statement. We will redact sensitive items but provide evidence as part of the security pack.
[06:23] Marcus: Are there any encryption-in-transit caveats? We must force TLS1.2+ and mutual TLS for internal connections.
[06:29] Marco: We enforce TLS 1.2/1.3 for API connections. Mutual TLS can be supported for private links/VPN endpoints on Dedicated/Private. We'll include config examples.
[06:41] Ellen: Logging volume is a cost factor — if we route audit logs to our S3, are there per-GB charges on your side?
[06:49] Marco: Not for Dedicated if you push logs directly to your endpoint; we don't charge per-GB for logs exported. For Hosted there may be egress charges depending on retention and storage. We'll surface cost estimates in the pilot plan.
[07:02] Priya: For GDPR, we need data subject rights ability — can we purge request-level transcripts for a user on request?
[07:10] Marco: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can support deletion APIs and we store user-level metadata to help with DSARs. Hosted can support deletions but cross-tenant forms occasionally complicate it; we'll outline the process and SLA.
[07:24] Ellen: Can you run through an example flow — support transcript for an EU user — what stays in-region, what logs, who can access keys?
[07:31] Marco: (walks through) Request hits eu API endpoint, request body is routed to Dedicated cluster in-region, temporary KVS and KV cache are in-region and ephemeral; transcripts are not logged to Redwood-managed storage if disabled, audit logs pushed to your S3 with KMS encryption under your key. Control plane metadata (billing, usage summary) can be summarized at org-level without PII and can be routed to central control plane if you allow.
[07:57] Marcus: Sounds good. Any red flags from your side? Latency requirements — we require 100ms p50 for small prompts in production.
[08:05] Marco: 100ms p50 is ambitious depending on model size; for smaller models and GPU types we can hit that. We should run a latency benchmark in the pilot. We'll propose a batching config and model selection (quantized smaller variant) to meet latency.
[08:21] Ellen: For the pilot, what dataset will you need from us? We don't want to send real PII.
[08:27] Marco: Use synthetic or redacted data for benching. For quality evals we can do a small approved in-scope dataset under DPA/BAA if necessary.
[08:36] Priya: On the topic of legal, can Redwood accept our standard CSAs or do we need to use Redwood's terms?
[08:41] Ava: For enterprise we can negotiate terms; we have a standard DPA and security addenda. Legal often goes back and forth but we try to accommodate customer-required clauses for regulatory needs.
[08:52] Ellen: Anything else on observability/audit? We need per-route cost breakdowns and token-level billing for audit.
[08:59] Marco: Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards and token-level cost breakdown. For Dedicated/Private we can push raw metrics into your observability stack (Prometheus/Grafana) and keep raw traces in-region.
[09:14] Marcus: One more: forensic access. If regulators request logs, what's the process and lead time?
[09:20] Ava: We'll support data export requests. For Dedicated/Private, you control the export. For Hosted, requests go through legal with our disclosure processes; we'll document timelines.
[09:33] Ellen: Ok recap and next steps?
[09:36] Ava: We'll send the SOC2, HIPAA mapping, and a Dedicated pilot plan (Ava/Marco) by Friday 2026-03-06. Ellen will share network topology and compliance scope by 2026-03-11. We'll schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-16.
[09:52] Priya: Sounds good. Thank you.
[09:55] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security pack and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[10:02] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache in system logs) and filler words. References to product names: Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Console, sometimes shortened to Redwood dedi or private control plane in the transcript. There are mentions of legal documents (DPA, BAA) and need for SOC2 and HIPAA artifacts.
